5.0.0.en: Stand fast therefore: the "therefore" completes the discourse with which the previous chapter ended, that the believers are children of Sarah the free woman and not children of bondage from the bondwoman. The word indicates their wavering. Freedom was given to them as a gift, and all that is required of them is to stand fast in it, for the slave does not abide in the house forever, but the son abides and inherits.

5.0.1.en: Be not entangled: do not turn aside from the upright faith and enslave yourselves to the ordinances and works of the Law. For this reason we find that worship in Christianity is in spirit and in truth. Fasts and prayers were established not to enslave man but to serve him, and through them he offers sacrifices of thanksgiving and praise to God with the love of sons and not the fear of slaves.

5.0.2.en: I Paul say unto you: that is, I am confident of what I say, that whoever clings to circumcision does not trust in the grace found in the blood of Christ the Savior alone, and consequently, by his unbelief, will not benefit from the salvation of Christ.

5.0.3.en: The Apostle calls them to be freed from the bondage of the Law and circumcision so that they may live with God in the Church in the freedom of sons.

5.1.0.en: Whoever among them commits himself to circumcision will be bound to keep the whole Law, because circumcision is linked with purification, offering sacrifices and keeping the Jewish ceremonies. Clinging to circumcision means returning from Christianity to Judaism and committing oneself to all its obligations, and a rejection of Christ. Consequently he warns the Galatians, who are Gentiles and believed in Christ, not to be circumcised as the false teachers, who are Jews converted to Christianity, call them to do.

5.2.0.en: Christ is become of no effect unto you: that is, you have made the work of Christ void in you.

5.2.1.en: Ye are fallen from grace: if man enslaves himself to the ordinances of the Law, grace forsakes him and he falls from eternal life, because grace is what keeps him standing in righteousness and holiness. Paul declares that whoever clings to circumcision and the Law will lose the salvation of Christ and the work of His grace in him.

5.2.2.en: Do not lose the work of God's grace in you by relying on material things or relationships, or by fearing the envy or power of people. On the contrary, persevere in your prayers even if the solution to your problems is delayed, confident of God's care and power.

5.3.0.en: By the Holy Spirit, whom we received by faith and who dwelt in us in Baptism, we have the hope of righteousness, of salvation to the end at the Second Coming. For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision nor separation avails anything, but faith which worketh by love. What is required is faith and not circumcision and the Law, but not theoretical faith; rather, faith that shows itself in works of love and mercy toward others.

5.4.0.en: Ye did run: it conveys activity and alertness.

5.4.1.en: Did hinder you: that is, obstructed you, so that you do not obey God who called you and turn aside from the way of truth by submitting to these deceivers, whose obedience is not from God.

5.4.2.en: A little leaven: what is meant is committing oneself to circumcision, which will lead them to complete Judaizing. The Apostle asks them what made them turn aside from the way of truth after they had been advancing on the way of grace. For a small error, if they do not quickly remedy it, will become a great danger.

5.4.3.en: Do not be lenient with a small sin lest it lead you to a greater one, because Satan most often draws you gradually into evil. So be careful and examine yourself every day in repentance together with your prayer, and take care to disclose all your sins and their causes in the sacrament of confession.

5.5.0.en: I have confidence in you through the Lord: he praises them and encourages them to correct their error, but our confidence must be in our God and not in ourselves.

5.5.1.en: That ye will be none otherwise minded: the Jews spread the word that the Apostle Paul preaches circumcision because he is a circumcised Jew and he allowed the circumcision of Timothy.

5.5.2.en: Shall bear his judgment: these deceivers have placed themselves under judgment because they are not in Christ.

5.5.3.en: Whosoever he be: whatever his position or fame.

5.5.4.en: Were even cut off: their separation from the teaching and from association with the believers in the Church.

5.5.5.en: After praising the Galatians, Paul denies that he has preached circumcision, and says, if I preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted by the Jews?..!! As for me, I preach only the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, which to the Jews is a stumbling block because it makes everyone equal, Jews and Gentiles, but the Jews want distinction. Would that these were cut off from the Church.

5.6.0.en: The Son has set us free, and we have become truly free from the bondage of sin by the power of God's grace, and from the Law of Moses by the power of the death of Christ for us. So do not use freedom to give free rein to the lusts of the flesh, but so that you may rise in spirit to a loftier thought and a higher level. For freedom in Christianity makes the believer enslave himself, by himself, to the service of others in love, and the thief no longer steals but labors and works to help the needy. So we are governed by the law of love.

5.7.0.en: Bite and devour: you harm and wound one another as an animal pounces on its prey to tear it and eat it.

5.7.1.en: If the sum of the Law is love for others, why do you walk in the opposite way, by condemning and exploiting one another? And by continuing these offenses and transgressions you destroy yourselves and draw away from God. If you bite and devour one another, where are you then from the law of love, and will circumcision benefit you?!

5.7.2.en: The goal of Christianity is love, which, as it grows toward God, appears in our dealings with others. And Satan tries to restrain our love with the preoccupations of sin and the cares of the world. When we are freed from them by repentance, we are released in love toward everyone. The proof of your freedom is the growth of your love toward others and your readiness to give even to the one who wrongs you.

5.8.0.en: Walk in the Spirit: submission to the Holy Spirit.

5.8.1.en: The Apostle Paul calls us to the spiritual walk and not to be led away after evil fleshly lusts.

5.9.0.en: The flesh: he means the evil fleshly lusts.

5.9.1.en: The Spirit: he means man's spirit submitted to the Holy Spirit.

5.9.2.en: The flesh, inclined to lusts, opposes the spiritual desires that his spirit seeks, and the spirit strives to bring man to life with God, but it is hindered by the flesh's attachment to lusts, so that when man desires with his spirit a pure relationship with God and people, his lustful flesh draws him by his laxity toward it, and he does the opposite of what he wants by the Spirit.

5.10.0.en: Those who are led by the Holy Spirit have every evil desire and lust quenched in them, and consequently they do not need the restraints of the Law, as often as they practice the means of grace that increase the work of the Holy Spirit in them, such as Communion, repentance, prayer and reading the Holy Bible; they have experienced the new life with Christ.

5.11.s.en: (5) The works of the flesh and the works of the Spirit

5.11.0.en: The works of the flesh, which refused to be led by the Holy Spirit, produce corruption, but if man submits his flesh to the leadership of the Holy Spirit, his life bears virtues by the work of the Holy Spirit. The Apostle Paul gave samples of sins, seventeen sins, which are divided into three categories:

5.11.1.en: 1- Six works for the gratification of the lusts of the flesh (adultery - uncleanness - lasciviousness - fornication): the use of sexual instincts for forbidden pleasure. Lasciviousness: the adultery of the married.

5.11.4.en: Revellings: a kind of rowdiness and wrath resulting from drunkenness.

5.11.6.en: Idolatry: not only by bowing down to idols, but the love of money is also considered a kind of idolatry (Col 3:5). Witchcraft: directly connected with Satan.

5.11.8.en: Hatred: hatred of another or stirring up enmities among people.

5.11.9.en: Variance: detesting another and shunning him.

5.11.10.en: Emulations: resentment of another's distinction over me, and I may seek to harm him.

5.11.11.en: Wrath: an outburst of anger and intense rage.

5.11.12.en: Strife: a faction that leads to division and to harming others.

5.11.15.en: Envyings: vindictiveness toward others and a grudge that cannot bear their success.

5.11.16.en: Murders: ending a life, or a moral murder by severe insult.

5.11.17.en: And whoever does such sins shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

5.12.0.en: He did not say fruits but the fruit of the Spirit, because they all come from one tree planted by the streams of the waters of the Holy Spirit. He mentions nine fruits of it, divided into three categories: 1) a hidden category that expresses the believer's state from within:

5.12.1.en: Love: the sign of being born from above: "We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren" (1 Jn 3:14). Joy: a joy that no one can take from the believer's heart and that is not affected by surrounding circumstances. Peace: the peace of God which passes all understanding fills the heart in the severest tribulations.

5.12.2.en: 2) A category that appears in the believer's relationship with others.

5.12.3.en: Longsuffering: by grace he acquires a superior ability to be patient and to bear the offenses of others, remembering our Lord's patience with him for his salvation.

5.12.4.en: Gentleness: dealing with meekness, compassion, kindness and forgiveness instead of harshness and roughness. Goodness: doing virtue in every situation with generosity and liberality.

5.12.6.en: Faith: believing in things unseen with complete trust in God, relying on Him and abiding in Him. Meekness: accepting offense from others with a broad heart like the Lord Christ, "learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart" (Mt 11:29), with quietness of voice and conduct.

5.12.7.en: Temperance: controlling the lusts of the flesh and sanctifying the senses and feelings to God.

5.12.8.en: Against such there is no law: God's law agrees with the preceding fruits, and if it says otherwise, it is not a law from God.

5.13.0.en: They that are Christ's: they are those who accepted Him as Lord, Redeemer and Savior and believed in Him.

5.13.1.en: The believers in Christ are His own, who followed Him and have put to death the lusts of the flesh by grace and by the power of the Holy Spirit.

5.14.0.en: If we live in the Spirit, that is, by the power of the Holy Spirit, it is fitting for us to walk according to the principles of the Spirit and to side with His leadership.

5.15.0.en: Whoever walks in the Spirit is not conceited, that is, proud, because the sin of pride leads to anger and selfishness; man wants everything for himself and envies others if they obtain something that he does not have.

5.15.1.en: As Christ left everything for your sake on the cross, would that you leave something of your comfort and material desires for His sake, that is, that you control your passions, repent of your sins, and give yourself an opportunity for prayer and for hearing His voice in the Holy Bible.

5.15.2.en: Compassion for sinners - giving to the teachers

6.0.0.en: Overtaken: that is, Satan overcame him and made him fall.

6.0.1.en: A man: to show human weakness.

6.0.2.en: Fault: that is, his feet slipped and he fell into sin.

6.0.3.en: The Apostle Paul began his epistle with rebuke, saying "O foolish", and ends it with gentleness, "brethren", in order to win everyone to Christ. For Christianity did not lay down ordinances and rulings but principles that lift the believers to what is higher than the law. So they, as spiritual people, if a man among them falls into a fault, must restore him and not judge him, that is, bring him back from his error in a spirit of meekness, gentleness and love, this meekness resulting from a humble heart, for love and gentleness are the greatest medicine for the fallen. He also warns the healer not to be proud lest he fall too, because we are no better than the one who fell.

6.1.0.en: Bear ye one another's burdens: bearing the repeated sins and offenses of others, guiding them, visiting them, praying for them and offering every means of love to win them.

6.1.1.en: Love does not stop at not condemning the fallen, but goes on to bear their burdens and falls and to help them, as Christ bore our shame. This is the law of Christ, that is, His commandments which the Apostle Paul commanded us to fulfill.

6.1.2.en: Do we raise up the fallen with meekness and love, or are we harsh toward them?! Let us remember our sins, and so bear with them and encourage them, confident that continuing love softens the hardest rejecting hearts.

6.2.s.en: (2) Let every man prove his own work

6.2.0.en: To be something: that is, he is proud and ascribes his works and glories to himself.

6.2.1.en: When he is nothing: considering that he is dust and ashes and falls into sins, and all his abilities are grace from God. Whoever is proud of the works he accomplishes, or his thoughts and words, forgetting that he is created from dust and that all his distinction is the work of God's grace in him, deceives himself, for he forgets his sins and weaknesses and steals God's glory for himself.

6.3.0.en: Let every man prove his own work: let him call himself to account before God and confess his sins before the priest. The Apostle Paul calls us to repentance instead of pride, so that man discovers his sins and is humbled and asks the help of God, who forgives him and supports him; and he boasts in the grace of God that supports him and is not proud toward others when he compares his good works with the shortcomings of others, because all these works are from God and not from himself.

6.4.0.en: In the end Paul affirms that every man is responsible for himself before God and will be called to account for all his works, so he should care for his repentance and not be occupied with comparing himself with others or being proud toward them, for this will not benefit him but will make him fall into sins that destroy him.

6.4.1.en: Be careful about your daily repentance before you sleep, for it cleanses you from all your sins and makes you humble before God, so you receive His mercies, and humble with people, so you win them.

6.5.s.en: (3) Whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap

6.5.0.en: Communicate: he shares the material goods between himself and his teacher, giving him a part of them to meet his needs.

6.5.1.en: Christ declared that "the labourer is worthy of his hire" (Lk 10:7), and consequently whoever learns the word of God should care for his teacher's material needs and provide them for him. This fellowship establishes love between the two, and humility as well, for each of them needs the other and receives from him.

6.6.0.en: Be not deceived: do not err and act in ignorance.

6.6.1.en: God is not mocked: no one can be proud against God by neglecting His commandments.

6.6.2.en: The Apostle Paul alerts the Galatians to the importance of generosity in giving, and even warns them against neglecting God's commandments by honoring the teachers and meeting their needs (Lk 10:7). What man offers of love to the teachers he will reap as happiness in heaven, based on the rule known among farmers, that whoever sows a good kind reaps good fruits, and the opposite is also true.

6.7.0.en: Paul confirms the meaning mentioned in the previous verse, that whoever refuses to give the teachers their material needs because he is busy with his fleshly lusts and selfishness will receive nothing, for the flesh will become dust and all the material lusts will pass away; indeed eternal torment awaits him because of his absorption in his lusts. But whoever cares for the spiritual work and for giving will be rewarded with glories in eternal life.

6.8.0.en: The Apostle Paul encourages us to continue to care for meeting the needs of the teachers and to do every good and mercy, and to persevere in that, because the complete result will appear in eternal life. For God in due season will bless us in part on earth so that we continue doing good, and fully in heaven so that we enjoy it forever.

6.9.0.en: Paul considers doing good an opportunity that the spiritual man should seize, so that he shows his love for God and for others and lays up for himself a treasure in heaven, and does good to every man, and especially to the believers, because he is more in contact with them and responsible for them; they are members with him in one body, which is the Church, while the unbelievers may find their needs met from others. His love and giving are for all, but he begins with the believers.

6.9.1.en: Doing good by helping others is a blessing to you before it is to the other. So do not turn away the one who asks you for something, especially if you are sure of his need; rather, would that you strive to provide for the needs of others, and care for those close to you, that is, your household and relatives and all those you live with, because you are responsible for them before God, not only in material things but rather in spiritual things, that is, the salvation of their souls and their attachment to the Church.

6.10.s.en: (4) The cross and the new creation

6.10.0.en: The Apostle Paul was accustomed to dictate his epistles to one of his helpers and then write a greeting at the end, or a signature, to confirm that he was the sender of the epistle. In the Epistle to the Galatians, however, he wrote the whole epistle or a large part of it with his own hand, and he wrote it in large letters because of his weak eyesight. His care for this epistle shows his emphasis on its meanings and its importance, and he asks those to whom he sent it to hold to it.

6.11.0.en: Paul speaks about the false teachers, who are Christians of Jewish origin and proclaim the necessity of circumcision to receive salvation. By this they please the Jews because they have added new members to Judaism, so that the Jews would not persecute them because of their conversion to Christianity, and would consider them concerned for Judaism since they convert the Gentiles to it by circumcision. This, of course, is a great error, because salvation is by the cross and the blood of Christ only and not by circumcision or by anything else.

6.12.0.en: The false teachers did not oblige those of the Christians of Gentile origin who were circumcised to the works of the Law, and were content with circumcision, for this meant the joining of the Gentiles to Judaism, so that the anger of the Jews would consequently be kept away from these teachers, since these teachers would be considered preachers of Judaism and not Christians who had left Judaism. They boast that they have circumcised, that is, joined many to Judaism.

6.13.0.en: The world is crucified unto me: since Paul believed in the cross, it made him die to fleshly lusts and to all the pride and grandeur of the world, so that he no longer seeks anything of them, for they were crucified to him, that is, died. And I unto the world: on the other hand, he became crucified to the world, that is, ready to bear sufferings and death for the sake of Christ in his preaching and his service to the world, to draw souls to faith.

6.13.1.en: The Apostle Paul declares his difference from the false teachers and that he does not seek any boasting in the material things of the world or in the opinions and approval of people, but, as an example to us, he boasts in the salvation he received through Christ the Redeemer on the cross.

6.14.0.en: Paul declares that salvation is not obtained by the uncircumcised, that is, the Gentiles, nor by the circumcised, that is, the Jews, but by the new creation, that is, those born again in the font of Baptism, who receive the new nature by which they live with God.

6.15.0.en: The Israel of God: what is meant is the Christian people.

6.15.1.en: Paul affirms the blessings granted to whoever lives by this sound thought, that is, faith in Christ the Savior, receiving Baptism, and not caring about circumcision. These blessings, which he expresses as God's grace and mercy, include all the believers among the Christians, for they are the new Israel who believed in the awaited Messiah, the Savior.

6.16.0.en: From henceforth let no man trouble me: no one can cast doubt on my apostleship and my following of Christ.

6.16.1.en: The marks of the Lord Jesus: the traces of the wounds and torments that Paul bore for Christ. Paul ends his speech by forbidding the Galatians to debate the subject of circumcision, to return to Judaism, and to follow the false teachers in their casting doubt on Paul's apostleship and faithfulness to Christ, and he offers the proof of his following of Christ, which is the marks of the torments visible in his body, which he bore for the sake of Christ. It is not merely a matter of discussions and argument; what matters is that we love Christ, who died for us, and bear everything for His sake.

6.17.0.en: Paul concludes his epistle by asking for the grace of God, in whom they believed, to be with their spirits and to bless them.

6.17.1.en: Control your lusts and bear insults for the sake of Christ, and then you will enjoy the blessings of the cross in your life, of reassurance, strength and joy; indeed, sufferings become a cause of blessing and pride, because they are your way to enjoy the abundant graces of God.
